description: Contact identity uniques cover live contacts only (owner ruling D-16, M12): migration 20261101000000_contact_partial_identity_uniques replaces the full uniques on contacts (business_id, email_normalized) and (business_id, phone_normalized) with SQL-only partial unique indexes WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, so a soft-deleted contact keeps its row but no longer blocks re-adding the customer, while two live contacts of one business still collide in the database and answer 409 contact_email_taken / contact_phone_taken. Run from apps/server: npx vitest run test/crm-contact-duplicate.integration.test.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/v1-17-vitest.json against a database migrated with prisma migrate deploy (never db push, which would drop the full uniques and create neither partial index) and REDIS_URL, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/contact-partial-unique.json --report .proof/v1-17-vitest.json. RED-BEFORE: at the tests-first commit c1981433 on a database with the old full indexes, 9 of the V1-17 cases fail (re-adding the customer of a soft-deleted contact answers 409 with existingContactId null; a P2002 naming the partial index is not mapped). Review repairs (CR-4, V117-ST-3) add the block 'V1-17 review repairs': revertMerge maps the P2002 of un-deleting a merged duplicate whose email or phone a live contact now holds to 409 contact_*_taken through the same visibility-bounded holder lookup, and any other restore failure answers 400 with no Prisma text. Against the V1-17 head 00a9f5f3 its four revert cases and the generic-400 case fail (400 carrying Prisma's invocation text), the positive control by cascade. CR-1 / V117-ST-2 (cancelForget meets the same P2002 and answers 500) needs contact-privacy.service.ts, outside this packet's write set, and is recorded as an it.todo in the same block. allowAdditionalCases is true because the suite also holds the R0-D7 cases bound by release0-landed.json and that it.todo; requireReportSuccess keeps every case of the file binding.
requiredCases: V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) the database holds each identity unique as a partial index over live rows, and no full unique on either column pair remains

V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) NEGATIVE CONTROL — the soft-deleted contact's phone is free too: POST with a punctuation variant answers 201 and the new contact is live

V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) a contact added again is recorded like any create (D-25): one ContactAuditEntry "created" naming the owner

V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) two live contacts still cannot share an identity: another POST of the email answers 409 contact_email_taken naming the live contact, of the phone 409 contact_phone_taken naming the live contact, never 500

V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) NEGATIVE CONTROL — PATCH of a live contact onto a soft-deleted contact's email and phone answers 200 and the live contact takes them

V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) two concurrent POSTs of one new email: exactly one 201 and one 409 contact_email_taken naming the winner (the database decides, not a read-then-write)

V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) the database refuses a second live holder: un-deleting the old contact while others hold its email and phone is a P2002, the row stays deleted, and rejectContactIdentityTaken maps that real error to 409 naming the live holder

V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) NEGATIVE CONTROL — a P2002 whose meta.target names a partial index instead of the column list still maps to 409 (email and phone); any other unique violation is rethrown untouched

V1-17 — a soft-deleted contact releases its email and phone: the identity uniques cover live contacts only (D-16) DRIFT GUARD — schema.prisma declares no unique on either pair and names both SQL-only indexes, the migrate-dev rule and the db-push ban at the Contact model; the migration creates exactly those partial indexes, drops the full ones and states the same rules

V1-17 review repairs — un-deleting a contact whose email or phone a live contact now holds (CR-4, V117-ST-3, CR-1, V117-ST-2) NEGATIVE CONTROL — within the undo window another contact takes the merged duplicate's email (201), and the revert answers 409 contact_email_taken naming that live contact, with no database text in the body; nothing is restored and the merge stays revertable

V1-17 review repairs — un-deleting a contact whose email or phone a live contact now holds (CR-4, V117-ST-3, CR-1, V117-ST-2) the revert's holder id is bounded by the actor's CRM visibility: a 'my book' STAFF who cannot open the holder gets the same 409 with existingContactId null and the id nowhere in the body

V1-17 review repairs — un-deleting a contact whose email or phone a live contact now holds (CR-4, V117-ST-3, CR-1, V117-ST-2) NEGATIVE CONTROL — the same for the phone: once the email is free again but a live contact holds a punctuation variant of the duplicate's phone, the revert answers 409 contact_phone_taken naming it

V1-17 review repairs — un-deleting a contact whose email or phone a live contact now holds (CR-4, V117-ST-3, CR-1, V117-ST-2) positive control — with both values free again the same revert succeeds: the duplicate is live with its email and phone, the merge is stamped reverted, and a second revert is refused 400
